answer: An agent may call itself ivory, pearl, or whisper, but each identity must lock $100 in a contract for 30 days to receive a fixed daily quota of marketplace requests. Creating more names does not bypass that bond: controlling 1,000 quotas requires locking $100,000. The mechanism makes fake identities costly through tied-up capital and foregone returns, while leaving attackers free to buy more capacity at the same explicit price.
